question: An ammeter is constructed by shunting a galvanometer of resistance $G$ with a small resistance $S$, so the ammeter has a finite internal resistance. This ammeter is inserted in series in a circuit whose remaining resistance (excluding the ammeter) is $R$, connected to an ideal voltage source. The true current without the ammeter would be $I_{true}$, while the current measured after inserting the ammeter is $I_{measured}$. Determine the fractional error $\frac{I_{true}-I_{measured}}{I_{true}}$ introduced due to the ammeter resistance.
